text.p: Argentina's Gabriela Sabatini called it quits on Thursday, announcing her immediate retirement after a 12-year career during which she won the 1990 U.S. Open and 26 other singles titles, a WTA statement said.

"I have made this decision after a long and well thought-out analysis, out of which has arisen my strong desire to pursue the development of other activities," Sabatini, 26, said in the statement issued by the WTA.
Sabatini played her last match last week, losing to Jennifer Capriati 6-3, 6-4 in the first round of the European Indoor Championships in Zurich, Switzerland.
Sabatini had been sidelined with a stomach injury for much of this year and missed both the French Open and Wimbledon. At the U.S. Open she lost in the third round.
Sabatini was ranked in the world's top ten from 1986 through 1995. She reached a high of number three in 1991 and 1992. She is currently ranked 29th in the world.
Sabatini earned nearly $9 million in prize money during her career. Her victory at the 1990 U.S. Open, by beating Steffi Graf 6-2, 7-6, was her only Grand Slam title.
